item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Investigating the Muscle-specific Power of thyroid hormone to ACTivate body metabolism (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The assignment is aimed at collaborating on the experimental activities envisaged by the IMPACT project, using genetically modified mouse models and primary cultures of muscle stem cells. Activities will include the characterization of the muscle phenotype under physiological and pathological conditions, the analysis of metabolic parameters and energy homeostasis, as well as the study of alterations associated with muscle atrophy. Molecular and cellular biology methodologies will also be used to evaluate metabolic adaptations and gene expression in response to the modulation of thyroid hormone action.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 12:00
Institution: INSUBRIA, Varese
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-01 Botanica

Morphological, histological, and biochemical analysis of leaves and roots of the native species Arrhenatherum elatius and Trifolium pratense, and the exotic species Broussonetia papyrifera and Robinia pseudoacacia, grown in contaminated soils under both natural and mesocosm conditions. Analysis of the phytostabilizing effect of biochar applied to contaminated soils and its impact on plant development.

Through multidisciplinary approaches, the project aims to advance our understanding of the bacterium Xylella fastidiosa subsp. pauca and its infection mechanisms, as well as plant defence responses and the molecular basis of plant–pathogen interactions. The research activities will involve extracting DNA from archaeological sediments dating from the final Middle Palaeolithic to the Initial Upper Palaeolithic and collected during excavations conducted within the ERC Last Neanderthals project. Sedimentary DNA will be analysed using methodologies and protocols specifically designed for archaeological samples. The data generated through the laboratory work will subsequently be processed, analysed, and validated. item.description:

Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The project will evaluate the biodistribution, biological activity and therapeutic efficacy of recombinant TAT?-CDKL5 protein in cellular and mouse models of CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder. Cellular studies will assess protein uptake, localization and persistence, together with effects on neuronal survival and maturation. Mouse studies will examine brain distribution, neuronal localization and pharmacodynamic responses to identify a dosing regimen for efficacy testing. Treatment effects will be assessed through behavioural testing and biochemical, histological and morphometric analyses, with particular attention to dendritic and synaptic alterations. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-07 Biochimica

The research will identify and characterise synthetic and natural molecules capable of counteracting mitochondrial dysfunction by modulating F1FO-ATPase and preserving respiratory supercomplex organisation. Biochemical, kinetic and bioenergetic analyses in isolated mitochondria and cellular models will assess the effects of selected compounds on ATP synthesis and hydrolysis, mitochondrial respiration, membrane potential, ROS production and calcium homeostasis. Respiratory supercomplex assembly and susceptibility to mitochondrial permeability transition will also be investigated. Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-11 Farmacologia

Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive central nervous system malignancy in adults. This research project aims to identify novel druggable molecular targets to advance differentiation therapy strategies for glioblastoma (GBM). By inducing terminal differentiation of glioma stem cells (GSCs) and converting stem-like cells into non-stem states sensitive to conventional treatments, this project aims to reduce tumor intrinsic dynamic plasticity and achieve effective GBM eradication.
